AVORA provides decision support. Disconnect power before electrical, pump or valve work, and always prioritize product labels, hardware limits and professional advice.
What order should I follow when setting up AVORA?

Verify garden information, location and units in Settings. Create zones and map sensors and valves in Zone Management. Calibrate sensors, then confirm current Raspberry Pi, ESP32 and measurement status in Device Health. Enable automatic irrigation only after these checks.
How do I move between the main screens?

The bottom navigation opens the primary sections. The main menu provides AI tools, statistics, watering history and season management. Quick Settings shows frequently used settings cards in the order you choose.
What do healthy, attention, critical and no-data mean?

Healthy means current data is within a safe range. Attention or critical asks you to review the explanation on that card. No data or waiting can mean the sensor is off, disconnected or stale; automatic decisions are restricted for safety.
Do existing records change when I change units?
Selections under Settings > Units change how values are displayed. Stored base values remain intact; temperature, area, volume and similar values are converted to the selected unit.
How do I customize Quick Settings?

Open editing in the Quick Settings section. Choose from garden, irrigation, sensors, product catalog, units, notifications, NAS and other settings cards. This changes shortcuts only and never removes the actual settings screens.
How do I add, edit or retire zones?

Configure up to eight zones under Settings > Zone Management. You can edit name, location, crop, icon, color, sensor, valve and irrigation settings. Retiring a zone preserves its history; it can be restored or its archive can be viewed.
How are sensors and valves assigned to zones?

Choose sensor and valve identifiers in the Connections section of Edit Zone. Enable physical valves from Irrigation Assistant settings. Verify every mapping against physical labels because an incorrect mapping can use another zone’s moisture or valve.
When should I calibrate a soil moisture sensor?

Calibrate after installing a new sensor, changing its position or soil type, or seeing values remain near 0 or 100. Automatic irrigation is safely stopped during calibration; complete the dry and wet reference steps in order.
How do I start and close a season?

Start a season for a zone from My Plants or Season Management. Verify crop, variety, planting date and initial details. At the end, enter the result and close it; active tracking stops while history and summaries remain available.
How do I open old seasons and retired-zone archives?
Use the season selector at the top of Plant Journal. Retired zones appear under Retired zone archives in Season Management. Closed seasons are read-only.
Can I edit or delete a journal record?

Tap a user-created journal record and edit or delete it from the detail screen. Automatic irrigation and fertilizer history are managed on their own screens. AI records show linked operations only when an explicit relation identifier matches.
Why does automatic irrigation not start?

The main system, automatic mode and zone irrigation must be enabled. The sensor must be current and stable, the physical valve ready, and pump cycle and cooldown limits valid. Weather and safety conditions are also checked; the pump stays off if any required condition is missing.
Why is it waiting even though moisture is low?

AVORA waits for water to spread through the root zone after irrigation. It also checks the stable-reading window, restart difference, cycle limit and rain effect. The decision explanation on the card identifies the pending condition.
How do I start manual watering?

Open the zone in Irrigation Assistant and choose Open manual watering. Set hours, minutes and seconds. The Pi opens the valve, waits for its safe opening time, runs the pump and closes both when time expires.
Where do I set manual duration and its upper limit?

Choose a duration whenever starting manual watering; the last value is remembered per zone. The shared safety maximum is under Irrigation Assistant > Settings > Manual watering safety. Use seconds mainly for short hardware tests.
How do I enable all eight valves?

Enable only zones with a physically connected relay and valve in Valve setup under Irrigation Assistant settings. Compare GPIO mappings with Raspberry Pi wiring. Confirm that software configuration matches LOW-trigger relay hardware.
What does Restart irrigation process erase?

It clears temporary decision windows, cycle locks and pending forecast validation for selected zones. Watering history, learned durations and safety cooldowns remain, and no pump or valve starts immediately. The operation is blocked during active watering.
Can weather forecast stop watering by itself?

No. AVORA first uses live soil moisture and safety conditions. Rain with sufficient probability and amount can delay a small moisture deficit; hot and dry weather can adjust a required duration within safe limits.
Where can I see the result and stop reason of watering?
Open Main menu > Watering History and filter by zone. Each record shows mode, duration, before and after moisture, change and stop reason. Statistics summarizes duration and success.
What is the difference between the four AI tools?

Plant Assistant evaluates photos and garden data. Seedling Assistant tracks batches and development. Fertilizer Assistant supports nutrition using products, stage, stock and past outcomes. Irrigation Assistant learns moisture response and watering results separately for each zone.
Where does a Plant Assistant analysis appear later?

A saved analysis is added to the related zone’s Plant Journal. Its photo, purpose, confidence, assessment and advice are stored as recorded. Open analysis record on the generated notification goes directly to that entry.
Does AI Plant Assistant work remotely?

Yes. The phone and Raspberry Pi do not need the same Wi-Fi when reachable through Tailscale. The NAS API and visual analysis service must be running on the Pi. If unavailable, check the error code and Tailscale status.
Does Plant Assistant provide a definitive diagnosis?

No. It provides probability and observation support. Clear, current photos from consistent angles and correct sensor data improve confidence. Consult an agronomist for serious, rapidly progressing or uncertain conditions.
How do I track a seedling batch and transfer it to a season?

Create a batch in Seedling Assistant and enter crop, variety, count, sowing date, stage and sensor mapping. Daily logs preserve sensor values at record time. When ready to plant, transfer it from batch details to create the target zone season.
How do I restore an archived seedling batch?

Open the archive filter or archived batches section in Seedling Assistant. Manually archived batches can be restored. Transferred batches remain linked to their season and provide Open linked season. Archived batches do not receive live sensor tracking.
Does Irrigation Assistant learn separately by zone?

Yes. Sensor response, moisture change, duration and results are evaluated per zone. Reliable learning needs correct calibration and enough completed cycles. Manual tests appear in history while automatic safety remains enforced.
Which records are added to Plant Journal automatically?

Completed irrigation, recorded fertilizer applications, AI analyses and selected system events are attached to the related zone and season. Observations, events, notes and growth photos can be added manually. Linked Records shows only explicitly related operations.
Does a fertilizer recommendation mean it was applied?

No. AVORA never applies fertilizer automatically. Check label, dose, growth stage, repeat interval and mixture safety. Record it only after actual application; history, next date and stock then update from that record.
How are fertilizer products and stock managed?

Enter product name, type, application unit, stock, label information and eligibility in Product Catalog. Single, bulk or mixed application reduces stock atomically. Unit mismatch or insufficient stock blocks the record.
How does Fertilizer Assistant learn from outcomes?

Use the outcome notification after application to record growth, vigor and notes. At least two reliable results for the same product and zone allow past patterns to support later advice. Learning never overrides labels, analysis or safety limits.
What are notifications for and how do I open the related item?

Notification Center collects irrigation results, plant analyses, fertilizer follow-ups, seedling warnings, device and access events. The action button opens the exact record or section when possible. Notification and reminder types are configured separately in Settings.
Which data is used by Statistics?
Statistics summarizes duration, success and moisture change from saved watering history. Older records without a zone can appear in overall totals; zone filters show only matching identifiers.
What happens if Raspberry Pi is on but sensors are offline?
Raspberry Pi and ESP32/sensor connectivity are monitored separately. ESP32 can lose power or network while Pi remains online. Automatic irrigation is blocked when current sensor data is unavailable.
What should I check in Device Health?

Check Pi reachability, API version, uptime, firmware versions, latest sensor time and data freshness. The application, Pi service and firmware are separate components; one can be current while another is old.
What should I do when NAS or AI shows no connection?

Check phone internet, then confirm avora-nas is online in Tailscale. The API health endpoint and secure HTTPS address on Pi must respond. After NAS restart, Tailscale state and Funnel configuration should return from persistent storage.
What should I consider when testing relays, valves or pump?
Disconnect power before changing wiring. Verify relay trigger type and valve/pump voltage and current. Start with one short valve test, never run the pump dry and keep the Pi safety timeout enabled.
Why does a new phone require device authorization?

Firebase and garden access are protected per device. Send the displayed authorization identifier to the administrator or request garden access through your NAS account. Reopen the app after approval; do not recreate an existing account with another invite.
How do I add a family member?

The administrator creates a one-time invite under Settings > NAS Account and Security. The family member creates a separate account with that code and requests garden access. The administrator approves it from the notification or Manage access requests.
How do I manage accounts, devices and inactive access?

NAS Account and Security lists accounts, this device and other open sessions. The administrator can close other sessions. If a family member does not connect for 30 days, the administrator can keep or remove garden access. The administrator account is excluded from this review.
What is the difference between Data Sync and Backup?

Sync keeps current data available across devices through Firebase and NAS. Backup exports a point-in-time portable data file and a separate photo ZIP. Synchronization does not replace backups; use both.
What should I back up before changing phones?

Create both a data backup and a photo ZIP from Data Sync and Backup. Data backup includes garden, zones, irrigation, seasons, journal, fertilizer, notifications and settings. Live sensor values, commands, access keys and photo files are excluded from the data file.
Does restore delete my current data?

Restore merges without deleting current records and avoids duplicate photos. The pump remains off and automatic irrigation is disabled for review. Verify zones, sensors, valves and irrigation settings after restoration.
How do I send a problem or suggestion?

Open Settings > Feedback, choose type and related area, then describe the issue. You may include diagnostics such as app version and phone model. Administrators track messages as unread, read and resolved in Feedback Inbox.
